Only network failure observed across all pages was the expected pre-login 401 on /api/auth/me.

minor.issue: Body is parsed as a raw dict with no Pydantic model. If the 'lines' key is missing/misnamed the endpoint returns 200 'Inbound updated' with empty deltas AND overwrites received_items with an empty list — a silent destructive no-op. Recommend a Pydantic model with a non-empty lines list.
These endpoints read request.json() untyped and have no 404 guard on arrival/qc (update_one on a non-existent id silently returns 200 'Arrival recorded').

_monthly_value() computes BILLING_MONTHS but never uses it (annual/12 always) — dead code that implies billing-frequency weighting that does not exist. Also renewal_rate_pct counts cancelled contracts in the denominator, so churn depresses the 'renewal rate' metric; confirm this is the intended definition.
Sequence numbers use count_documents({})+1, so soft-deleted/renewed rows can produce duplicate asset_code/contract_number under concurrency. Use a counters collection or findAndModify.

critical_code_review_comments: server.py is 6,850 lines — well past the 700-line guidance; the inbound/import blocks touched in this iteration are good candidates to extract into purchase_inbound.py and inventory_import routes alongside the already-extracted assets/amc/locations routers.

locations.location_scope_filter returns {} for admins and for users with no scope, so read-filtering silently no-ops for every existing user until locations are assigned — acceptable for the approved scoped implementation but worth an explicit note in the UI.

Untyped `payload: Dict[str, Any]` bodies on PUT /locations/{id}, PUT /assets/{id}, PUT /amc/contracts/{id} allow arbitrary field injection into the documents (only _id/id are stripped); consider allow-lists.

rca_of_the_issue:
No blocking defects. Root cause of the two reported issues: (1) AssetsPage detail dialog composes a shadcn Badge (div) inside a

, which React flags as invalid DOM nesting; (2) edit_inbound reads an untyped request.json(), so a body without the 'lines' key produces an empty loop and then unconditionally $sets received_items to [] while returning 200 — the frontend never hits this because it always sends 'lines', but any other caller (or a future refactor) would silently wipe the receipt record.
